title: Three perfect days in Las Vegas: the Eagles, red rock and the week before the race
dek: Downtown history on Friday, Valley of Fire and Chinatown on Saturday, and a Sunday of football, pinball and a wheel over the Strip, while Formula 1 builds its track around you.

hero.caption: Sphere, east of the Strip, where the Eagles play Friday and Saturday night.

intro:
Las Vegas spends this weekend getting ready for a bigger one. The Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix runs Thursday to Saturday, Nov. 19 to 21, and the setup is already in the streets: grandstands and barriers along the Strip, overnight lane reductions, and from early Saturday Koval Lane closed behind the east-side resorts. None of it stops a weekend here, but it does change how you plan one, which is why this guide keeps Friday downtown and Saturday mostly off the Strip.

What's on is a good spread. The Latin Grammys fill MGM Grand Garden Arena on Thursday night, and the Eagles return to Sphere on Friday and Saturday for two of the last dates of their long residency. Saturday also brings Teddy Swims to T-Mobile Arena and the girl group KATSEYE to MGM Grand. On Sunday the Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium in the afternoon and the Golden Knights play the Vancouver Canucks that evening.

Mid-November is also the start of the desert's best season. The trails at Valley of Fire, closed through the summer heat, have been open since October, the days are mild, and the sun sets around 4:30, so outdoor plans belong in the morning. The plan below goes from the Mob Museum and the Neon Boneyard on Friday, to red sandstone and hand-pulled noodles on Saturday, to brunch facing the Bellagio fountains and a night ride on the High Roller on Sunday.

days.title: Friday: downtown and the Arts District
days.intro: Start with coffee on Main Street, spend the day on the stories that made the city, and finish with steak and a drink in the oldest bars and dining rooms downtown.

stops.name: Makers & Finders
stops.text: Josh Molina's Latin cafe is where the Arts District starts its day. Order a Cuban cortado or a lavender latte with the chilaquiles or the Latin hash, and sit long enough to watch Main Street wake up around the antique shops and breweries. It is a good first meal for a long day on foot. Practical note: it is a five-minute walk from Esther's Kitchen, where you will be back for lunch, and about ten minutes by car to the Mob Museum.

stops.name: The Mob Museum
stops.text: The National Museum of Organized Crime and Law Enforcement fills a 1933 federal courthouse, and the courtroom where the Kefauver hearings were held in 1950 is part of the visit. Give it two hours: three floors cover the mob's hold on the casinos and the agents who broke it. In January the museum opened *Filmed in Las Vegas*, on how Hollywood shaped the city's image. Practical note: the museum opens daily at 9 a.m., and the Underground speakeasy and distillery in the basement opens at 11.

stops.name: Esther's Kitchen
stops.text: James Trees opened Esther's in 2018 and moved it into a larger room on South Main in 2024; it is still the restaurant locals send visitors to. The kitchen calls its food seasonal Italian soul food: order the cacio e pepe or the signature rigatoni, and a margherita or duck confit pizza for the table. Lunch is the easier booking, since dinner reservations are hard to get. Practical note: reserve a day or two ahead, even for lunch on a Friday.

stops.name: The Neon Museum
stops.text: The Neon Boneyard keeps the signs the city took down: casino letters, motel arrows and giant figures, laid out in an open-air lot under the desert sky. Daylight lets you read the paint, rust and craftsmanship that the night hides, and the History Tour add-on explains where each sign once stood. Practical note: daytime admission runs 3 to 5 p.m. daily, with last entry at 4:30 and about 45 minutes inside. Phones are fine for photos, but cameras are not allowed.

stops.name: Hugo's Cellar
stops.text: Down a flight of stairs from the Four Queens casino floor, Hugo's Cellar serves the kind of dinner Las Vegas served before celebrity chefs: a salad made at the table and included with the entree, a ribeye or filet, a Beef Wellington, and desserts flamed tableside. It is dark, plush and unhurried, which is the point. Practical note: dinner runs nightly from 5 to 10 p.m., and Friday tables go, so book ahead.

stops.name: Atomic Liquors
stops.text: Opened in 1954, Atomic is the city's oldest freestanding bar, and it holds Nevada's Tavern Sale License No. 00001, which hangs behind the bar. The story goes that 1950s regulars watched the atomic tests from the roof. Closed in 2010 and reopened in 2012, it now pours well-made cocktails in a room that still looks the part. Practical note: it is a 15-minute walk east along Fremont from the Four Queens, or a short ride if you would rather not cross under the canopy crowds.

days.title: Saturday: Valley of Fire and Chinatown
days.intro: Drive an hour north for the red sandstone while the morning is cool, then come back for noodles, a tiki bar and dinner on Spring Mountain Road before the Eagles.

stops.name: Valley of Fire State Park
stops.text: Nevada's oldest state park is a landscape of red Aztec sandstone, petroglyphs and slot canyons about an hour from the Strip on I-15. The trails closed through the summer heat, including the Fire Wave, White Domes and Pastel Canyon, reopened on Oct. 1, and mid-November is when they are at their best. Walk the Fire Wave first, then White Domes, and stop at the visitor center for the maps. Practical note: day use is $15 per car with out-of-state plates, $10 for Nevada plates, with no reservation; the visitor center keeps 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. hours. Check the park site before you go, since a temporary closure of the west entrance is posted.

stops.name: Shang Artisan Noodle
stops.text: Back in town, eat at the original Shang, on the Review-Journal's 2025 list of the city's 100 best restaurants. The noodles are pulled or knife-shaved to order: get the beef noodle soup or the knife-shaved noodles in pork rib soup, plus the spicy wontons and the cold sesame noodles. It is fast, cheap and exactly what you want after a desert hike. Practical note: there are no reservations; the line forms at the 11 a.m. opening, so a mid-afternoon arrival is easier.

stops.name: The Golden Tiki
stops.text: A strip-mall door in Chinatown opens onto a dark, kitschy tiki room that has become one of the city's favorite bars, and it runs one of the best rum menus off the Strip. Order a Painkiller or a mai tai, and a plate of coconut shrimp or crab Rangoon to tide you over. Practical note: happy hour runs daily from 4 to 7 p.m., the right window before dinner, and the room fills quickly on a Saturday.

stops.name: Sparrow + Wolf
stops.text: Brian Howard left the Strip to open Sparrow + Wolf in Chinatown in 2017, and it remains one of the reasons locals eat off-Strip. The menu pulls from all over Asia and the Mediterranean: the oxtail hummus is the most-ordered dish, with oysters, the banh cuon and a carpaccio worth a look. Practical note: it opens at 4:30 p.m. daily for dinner only; book an early table so you can make Sphere by 8.

stops.name: Eagles at Sphere
stops.text: The Eagles have played Sphere since 2024, and Friday and Saturday are two of six fall dates the band added in May. The hits play out under the venue's wraparound interior screen, among the largest and sharpest LED displays anywhere, so the setting is half the show. Practical note: the show starts at 8:30 p.m.; F1 work has taken Sands Avenue bus stops out of service, so take a ride to the Venetian side and walk the bridge.

days.title: Sunday: the Center and South Strip
days.intro: Brunch across from the fountains, the Raiders in the afternoon, a few quarters' worth of pinball, then Italian at Aria and the High Roller after dark.

stops.name: Mon Ami Gabi
stops.text: Mon Ami Gabi's sidewalk patio, under the Paris Eiffel Tower, looks straight across the Strip to Bellagio's lake, which is why people wait for it. Weekend brunch runs 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. Friday through Sunday: eggs Benedict, French toast, corned beef hash and a smoked-salmon platter, with a cafe au lait or a glass of rosé. Practical note: book through OpenTable and ask for the patio. On a game day, eat at opening and leave by noon.

stops.name: Raiders vs. Seattle Seahawks
stops.area: Allegiant Stadium, west of the South Strip
stops.text: The Raiders host Seattle at 1:05 p.m. in Week 10, and Allegiant Stadium, the black dome west of Mandalay Bay, is worth seeing from the inside even if you do not follow either team. Expect a big Seahawks crowd, since Seattle is a short flight away. Practical note: you can walk from Mandalay Bay or Luxor over the Hacienda Avenue bridge across I-15; ride-share lots fill and clear slowly, so allow time after the game.

stops.name: Pinball Hall of Fame
stops.addr: Las Vegas Blvd. S., just south of the Welcome sign
stops.text: A nonprofit warehouse just south of the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign, with hundreds of playable pinball machines and classic arcade games from every decade. Entry is free; most games cost 25 cents to $1, so a $10 bill buys an hour of play. It is the least pretentious room on the Strip and a good way to wind down after a game. Practical note: it is open until 9 p.m. on Sundays.

stops.name: Carbone
stops.text: Mario Carbone's red-sauce restaurant brought New York's Greenwich Village scene to Aria, and it still runs on the same set pieces: spicy rigatoni vodka, veal Parmesan and a Caesar salad made at the table. It is loud, expensive and a lot of fun. Practical note: dinner runs nightly from 5 to 10 p.m.; Carbone is not on OpenTable, so book through Aria's restaurant pages or by phone.

stops.name: High Roller
stops.text: The High Roller, the 550-foot observation wheel behind the LINQ Promenade, takes about 30 minutes to make one turn, and at night the whole Strip lays out below you, Sphere glowing just to the east. Choose the standard cabin or the one with an open bar. Practical note: buy tickets online for a set time; from Aria it is a 10-minute ride or a 25-minute walk north.

stay.name: Four Seasons Hotel Las Vegas
stay.text: No casino and no smoke: the Four Seasons occupies its own floors at the top of Mandalay Bay, with a private pool and entrance, but shares the resort's restaurants and walkway. It is a short walk to Allegiant Stadium for Sunday, and the South Strip sits outside most of the F1 setup work.

stay.name: Caesars Palace
stay.text: Sixty years on, still the Strip's best address for the old-Vegas experience: fountains, columns and the Forum Shops, with the Colosseum inside. It puts you a short walk from Paris, Bellagio and the High Roller for Sunday, though Strip traffic slows as the race nears.

stay.name: Golden Nugget
stay.text: The best-kept of the downtown classics, with a pool built around a shark tank and the Mob Museum, Hugo's Cellar and Atomic Liquors all within walking distance for Friday. Downtown rates are lower than the Strip's, and the F1 closures are nowhere near.

events.name: Latin Grammy Awards
events.text: The 27th Latin Grammys bring Daddy Yankee, Rosalía, Karol G and Anitta to the stage; Edgar Barrera leads the nominations with 10. Expect a crowded MGM Grand on Thursday.

events.name: Eagles at Sphere
events.text: Two of six fall dates the band added to its Sphere residency; the last two follow on Nov. 27 and 28.

events.name: Teddy Swims: The Ugly Tour
events.text: The soul singer behind 'Lose Control' brings his arena tour to the Strip for one night.

events.name: KATSEYE: The Wildworld Tour
events.text: The global girl group formed on a reality competition series brings its arena tour to MGM Grand.

events.name: Formula 1 setup: Koval Lane closes
events.where: Koval Lane between Rochelle and Harmon avenues
events.text: Ahead of the Grand Prix on Nov. 19 to 21, Koval closes fully behind the east-side resorts; Strip and Sands Avenue lane reductions run overnight through Friday.

events.name: Raiders vs. Seattle Seahawks
events.text: Week 10 of the NFL season, and a rare visit from Seattle.

events.name: Golden Knights vs. Vancouver Canucks
events.text: Vegas hosts Vancouver in the team's 10th season; the Knights also host Nashville on Friday at 7 p.m.

know: **From the airport.** Harry Reid International (LAS) is just south of the Strip, 10 to 20 minutes away by taxi. Taxis charge flat zone fares to Strip hotels, about $21 to $29 depending on how far north you go, plus a card fee; Uber and Lyft pick up in the Terminal 1 and Terminal 3 garages.

**Getting around.** The Deuce bus runs the length of the Strip to downtown 24 hours a day; a 24-hour pass is $8 and a three-day pass $20 in the rideRTC app. The Monorail runs behind the east side of the Strip from MGM Grand to SAHARA.

**F1 setup.** The Grand Prix runs Nov. 19 to 21. Through Friday morning, the Strip loses lanes between Spring Mountain and Harmon from midnight to noon, and Sands Avenue overnight; Koval Lane closes fully from early Saturday. The Bellagio-to-Horseshoe and Harmon pedestrian bridges close from midnight to 9 a.m. through Saturday, and several Sands Avenue and Koval bus stops are out of service.
**Saturday needs a car.** Valley of Fire is about an hour northeast on I-15 with no transit; rent a car for the day. Leave by 8 to have the trails before the midday sun.
**Short days.** Sunset comes around 4:30 p.m. in mid-November, and desert evenings are cool. Carry a layer for Sphere and the High Roller.

**Big Saturday night.** The Eagles, Teddy Swims and KATSEYE all play Saturday, on top of Strip lane work, so expect long ride-share waits after 10 p.m. T-Mobile Arena allows only small clutches, no backpacks.
**Tipping.** 18 to 20 percent at sit-down restaurants, a dollar or two a drink at the bar, and something for housekeeping, valets and bell staff.
